# N Mate

Count along the ray by the clue digit. That target digit plus the clue equals the cage total. Cage digits are different.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| cell | The clue cell. | Required. |
| ray | The cells along the ray, nearest first. | Required. |
| cage | The cells in the cage. | Required. |

## Maths

Class: **with aggregates**.

The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate.

```text
let n=D(cell); 1<=n<=|ray| ∧ n+D(ray[n-1])=sum_D(cage) ∧ distinct_D(cage)
```

The marked digit names a one-based position within ray. The marked and target digits sum to the cage total. Cage digits are distinct.

## Example

````markdown
---
format: open-rules
title: N Mate example
setter: Example
source: ""
case: ""
library: https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/
status: read
---

```rules
sudoku 9x9
n-mate cell "r1c1" ray ["r1c2","r1c3"] cage ["r1c4"]
```
````

Satisfies the rule: r1c4=3, r1c1=1, r1c2=2, r1c3=4. The clue and its selected ray digit add up to the cage total.

Breaks the rule: r1c4=4, r1c1=1, r1c2=2, r1c3=4. The selected ray digit gives the wrong total.

---
name: Killer cage
url: https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/cage.md
kind: cage
parameters:
  cells:
    description: The marked cells, for example r1c1-r1c2-r2c2.
    default: Required.
    type: set<cell>
  total:
    description: The total the digits or values must add up to.
    default: No total imposed.
    type: optional<number>
  repeats:
    description: Whether repeated digits are allowed.
    default: false (distinct digits).
    type: boolean
  channel:
    type: Channel
    description: Read printed digits (D) or effective values (V).
    default: V.
---

# Killer cage

Cage digits add up to the stated total value. Digits are different unless repeats are allowed. A cage without a total supplies the repeat rule alone.

Omit `total` for a cage with no printed sum. A blank clue is not a total of zero. Use `total 0` only when zero is the required total. With `repeats true` and no total, this declaration adds no restriction.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| cells | The marked cells, for example r1c1-r1c2-r2c2. | Required. |
| total | The total the digits or values must add up to. | No total imposed. |
| repeats | Whether repeated digits are allowed. | false (distinct digits). |
| channel | Read printed digits (D) or effective values (V). | V. |

## Maths

Class: **with aggregates**.

The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate.

```text
(¬repeats → distinct_D(cells)) ∧ (present(total) → aggregate(cells,channel,"sum")=unwrap(total))
```

Face digits differ unless repeats are allowed. The selected channel supplies the optional total.

## Example

````markdown
---
format: open-rules
title: Killer cage example
setter: Example
source: ""
case: ""
library: https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/
status: read
---

```rules
sudoku 9x9
cage r1c1-r1c2 total 3
```
````

Satisfies the rule: r1c1=1, r1c2=2. The different digits 1 and 2 total 3.

Breaks the rule: r1c1=1, r1c2=3. The digits 1 and 3 total 4 instead of 3.

# Parity Cells

Values in the marked cells have the stated parity: odd or even.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| parity | The required parity: odd or even. | Required. |
| cells | The marked cells, for example r1c1-r1c2-r2c2. | Required. |

## Maths

Class: **first-order**.

The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate.

```text
∀c∈cells: ⌊V(c)⌋=V(c) ∧ (parity="odd" → odd(V(c))) ∧ (parity="even" → rem(V(c),2)=0)
```

Every V value has parity named by parity: odd has absolute remainder 1, even remainder 0 modulo 2.

## Example

````markdown
---
format: open-rules
title: Parity Cells example
setter: Example
source: ""
case: ""
library: https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/
status: read
---

```rules
sudoku 9x9
parity-cells r1c1-r1c2 parity "odd"
```
````

Satisfies the rule: r1c1=1, r1c2=3. Both marked digits are odd.

Breaks the rule: r1c1=1, r1c2=2. A marked cell contains the even digit 2.

---
name: Relation Scope
url: https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/relation-scope.md
kind: relation-scope
shape: Global
parameters:
  cells:
    type: set<cell>
    description: The bounded cell scope.
    default: Required.
  relations:
    type: list<PairRelation>
    description: Inclusive alternatives for each selected pair.
    default: Required.
  mode:
    type: enum{all,moves,incident}
    description: Select all pairs, move neighbours, or move neighbours incident to anchors.
    default: moves.
  move:
    type: Move
    description: The neighbour move.
    default: orthogonal.
  anchors:
    type: set<cell>
    description: Cells incident to covered edges.
    default: Empty set.
  except:
    type: list<list<cell>>
    description: Undirected pairs exempt from the condition.
    default: Empty list.
  negative:
    type: boolean
    description: Forbid every alternative on selected pairs.
    default: false.
  channel:
    type: Channel
    description: Read printed digits (D) or effective values (V).
    default: D.
---

# Relation Scope

Every selected pair satisfies at least one listed relation. With `negative true`, it fails every listed relation. All pairs stay inside `cells`; incident scope also requires at least one endpoint in `anchors`. Exceptions are undirected. Directed relations such as `less` follow increasing board cell order.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| cells | The bounded cell scope. | Required. |
| relations | Inclusive alternatives for each selected pair. | Required. |
| mode | Select all pairs, move neighbours, or move neighbours incident to anchors. | moves. |
| move | The neighbour move. | orthogonal. |
| anchors | Cells incident to covered edges. | Empty set. |
| except | Undirected pairs exempt from the condition. | Empty list. |
| negative | Forbid every alternative on selected pairs. | false. |
| channel | Read printed digits (D) or effective values (V). | D. |

## Maths

Class: **first-order**.

The [shared predicates](predicates.md) define the notation and operations.

```text
(∀p∈except: |p|=2) ∧ ∀a,b∈cells: cellIndex(a)<cellIndex(b) ∧ selectedPair(a,b,cells,mode,move,anchors) ∧ ¬graphEdge(except,a,b) → (if negative then ¬relatedAny(relations,read(a,channel),read(b,channel)) else relatedAny(relations,read(a,channel),read(b,channel)))
```

## Example

````markdown
---
format: open-rules
title: Relation Scope example
setter: Example
source: ""
case: ""
library: https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/
status: read
---

```rules
sudoku 9x9
relation-scope cells ["r1c1","r1c2"] relations [{"op":"difference","value":1},{"op":"sum","value":10}]
```
````

Satisfies the rule: Digits 3 and 7 total 10.

Breaks the rule: Digits 3 and 5 satisfy neither alternative.

name: Between
url: https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/between.md
kind: between
parameters:
  ends:
    description: The two end cells, in their stated order.
    default: Required.
    type: list<cell>
  line:
    description: The cells in order, for example r1c1-r1c2-r1c3.
    default: Required.
    type: path<cell>
---

# Between

Every digit between the ends is strictly greater than the smaller end and strictly less than the larger end.

The `line` lists only the cells between the two ends; `ends` lists the circles. Interior digits may repeat when other rules allow. They need not increase or decrease along the line.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ends | The two end cells, in their stated order. | Required. |
| line | The cells in order, for example r1c1-r1c2-r1c3. | Required. |

## Maths

Class: **first-order**.

The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate.

```text
|ends|=2 ∧ ∀c∈line: numericBetween(D(c),D(ends[0]),D(ends[1]),false)
```

Every interior digit lies strictly between the endpoint digits.

## Example

````markdown
---
format: open-rules
title: Between example
setter: Example
source: ""
case: ""
library: https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/
status: read
---

```rules
sudoku 9x9
between r1c2 ends ["r1c1","r1c3"]
```
````

Satisfies the rule: r1c2=2, r1c1=1, r1c3=3. 2 lies strictly between end digits 1 and 3.

Breaks the rule: r1c2=4, r1c1=1, r1c3=3. 4 is outside the interval between 1 and 3.

# Scoped Move

For the listed digits and chess move, prohibit either equal digits or consecutive digits in the related cells.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| move | The chess move connecting the compared cells. | Required. |
| relation | The prohibited relationship: equal values or values one apart. | Required. |
| digits | The allowed or required digits, listed explicitly; repeats in the list count where the rule says so. | Required. |
| scope | Compare only pairs whose two cells belong to this scope. | C (the whole board). |
| channel | Read printed digits (D) or effective values (V). | D. |

## Maths

Class: **first-order**.

The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate.

```text
scopedMove(move,relation,digits,scope,channel)
```

Either endpoint must have a listed face digit; both endpoints must be in scope. The selected channel supplies the compared numbers.

## Example

````markdown
---
format: open-rules
title: Scoped Move example
setter: Example
source: ""
case: ""
library: https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/
status: read
---

```rules
sudoku 9x9
scoped-move move "knight" relation "same" digits [1]
```
````

Satisfies the rule: r1c1=1, r2c3=6. The specified digit does not repeat across a knight move.

Breaks the rule: r1c1=1, r2c3=1. The specified digit repeats across a knight move.

name: Coordinate Count
url: https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/coordinate-count.md
kind: coordinate-count
shape: Cells
parameters:
  sources:
    type: list<cell>
    description: Source occurrences supplying coordinate indices.
    default: Required.
  scope:
    type: set<cell>
    description: Allowed destination cells.
    default: Required.
  rowBase:
    type: number
    description: Zero-based row before adding the transformed index.
    default: 0.
  colBase:
    type: number
    description: Zero-based column before adding the transformed index.
    default: 0.
  rowFactor:
    type: number
    description: Multiply the offset index by this row coefficient.
    default: 0.
  colFactor:
    type: number
    description: Multiply the offset index by this column coefficient.
    default: 1.
  offset:
    type: number
    description: Add this integer before applying the coordinate coefficients.
    default: -1.
  indexChannel:
    type: Channel
    description: Channel supplying the coordinate index.
    default: D.
  channel:
    type: Channel
    description: Channel supplying destination numbers.
    default: D.
  target:
    type: number
    description: The destination comparison target.
    default: Required.
  relation:
    type: PairRelation
    description: Relation from the destination number to the target.
    default: difference 0 (equal).
  total:
    type: position
    description: Required number of successful source occurrences.
    default: Required.
---

# Coordinate Count

Transform each source number into a board coordinate and count successful destinations. Add the offset, multiply by the row and column coefficients, then add the base coordinates. A whole-number index hits only when its destination belongs to scope and satisfies the stated relation with the target. Fractional indices and destinations outside scope are misses. Repeated source occurrences count separately.

The bases, coefficients and offset must all be integers.

The defaults index across the first row using one-based source numbers. Negative factors reverse a direction; setting both factors to zero selects one fixed destination for every integer source number.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| sources | Source occurrences. | Required. |
| scope | Allowed destinations. | Required. |
| rowBase, colBase | Zero-based base coordinate. | 0, 0. |
| rowFactor, colFactor | Coefficients of the offset index. | 0, 1. |
| offset | Integer added before scaling. | -1. |
| indexChannel | Index channel. | D. |
| channel | Destination channel. | D. |
| target | Destination comparison target. | Required. |
| relation | Destination-to-target relation. | difference 0 (equal). |
| total | Required hit count. | Required. |

## Maths

Class: **with aggregates**.

The [shared predicates](predicates.md) define coordinate hits and shared pair relations.

```text
⌊rowBase⌋=rowBase ∧ ⌊colBase⌋=colBase ∧ ⌊rowFactor⌋=rowFactor ∧ ⌊colFactor⌋=colFactor ∧ ⌊offset⌋=offset ∧ total=countWhere(sources,λs:cell:coordinateHit(s,scope,rowBase,colBase,rowFactor,colFactor,offset,indexChannel,channel,target,relation))
```

## Example

````markdown
---
format: open-rules
title: Coordinate Count example
setter: Example
source: ""
case: ""
library: https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/
status: read
---

```rules
sudoku 9x9
coordinate-count sources ["r2c1"] scope ["r1c1","r1c2"] target 7 total 1
```
````

Satisfies the rule: r2c1=2 and r1c2=7. The destination is the second cell of the first row.

Breaks the rule: r2c1=3. The destination falls outside scope.

# Slow Thermo

Digits never decrease from the bulb to the tip. Equal neighbours are allowed.

List the path from bulb to tip. The rule reads printed digits and permits repeats when other rules allow; a strict [Thermo](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/thermo.md) instead compares effective values with a strict increase.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| line | The cells in order, for example r1c1-r1c2-r1c3. | Required. |
| orientation | The increasing direction of the whole line. | forward. |
| channel | Read printed digits (D) or effective values (V). | D. |

## Maths

The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate.

This is a shorthand for [thermo](thermo.md). Its header binds the canonical parameters; its own parameters retain the defaults listed above.

The shared monotonic predicate permits equal neighbours.

## Example

````markdown
---
format: open-rules
title: Slow Thermo example
setter: Example
source: ""
case: ""
library: https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/
status: read
---

```rules
sudoku 9x9
slow-thermo r1c1-r1c2
```
````

Satisfies the rule: r1c1=2, r1c2=2. Equal neighbours do not decrease.

Breaks the rule: r1c1=2, r1c2=1. The second digit is smaller than the bulb.

name: Summit
url: https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/summit.md
kind: summit
parameters:
  line:
    empty_when: edges
    description: The cells in order, for example r1c1-r1c2-r1c3.
    default: Required.
    type: path<cell>
  loop:
    description: Whether the line closes, joining its last cell back to its first.
    default: false (open path).
    type: boolean
  edges:
    type: optional<list<list<cell>>>
    description: All edges of one connected network.
    default: Absent; use the ordered line.
---

# Summit

Neighbouring digits differ. Digits rise or fall along the line, changing direction only at 1 or 9.

With explicit `edges`, supply one connected network and write `line []` when no ordered list is needed. The window checks include every simple traversal through its junctions.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| line | The cells in order, for example r1c1-r1c2-r1c3. | Required. |
| loop | Whether the line closes, joining its last cell back to its first. | false (open path). |
| edges | All edges of one connected network. | Absent; use the ordered line. |

## Maths

Class: **with aggregates**.

The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate.

```text
lineGeometry(line,edges,loop)
∧ (∀W∈lineWindows(line,edges,2,loop): |W|=2 → D(W[0])!=D(W[1]))
∧ ∀W∈lineWindows(line,edges,3,loop): |W|=3 →
  ((D(W[1])∈{1,9} → (D(W[1])-D(W[0]))*(D(W[2])-D(W[1]))<0)
  ∧ (D(W[1])∉{1,9} → (D(W[1])-D(W[0]))*(D(W[2])-D(W[1]))>0))
```

Neighbouring digits differ. At each internal position the two successive differences have the same sign unless its digit is 1 or 9, where the sign reverses. A loop checks all positions cyclically.

## Example

````markdown
---
format: open-rules
title: Summit example
setter: Example
source: ""
case: ""
library: https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/
status: read
---

```rules
sudoku 9x9
summit r1c1-r1c2-r1c3
```
````

Satisfies the rule: r1c1=2, r1c2=9, r1c3=3. 2, 9, 3 changes direction at 9.

Breaks the rule: r1c1=2, r1c2=8, r1c3=3. 2, 8, 3 changes direction at 8.

# Index Count

Count successful lookups from the source occurrences. A fractional or out-of-range index is a miss. A hit compares the looked-up number with the target using the shared pair relation. Coordinate transforms can supply ordered strips to the same bounded `indexHit` predicate.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| sources | Index cells; repeated occurrences count separately. | Required. |
| cells | Cells in one-based lookup order. | Required. |
| target | The comparison target. | Required. |
| relation | Relation from each lookup result to the target. | difference 0 (equal). |
| indexChannel | Channel supplying each index. | D. |
| offset | Offset added before bounded lookup. | 0. |
| total | Required number of successful lookups. | Required. |
| channel | Read printed digits (D) or effective values (V). | D. |

## Maths

Class: **with aggregates**.

The [shared predicates](predicates.md) define the notation and operations.

```text
total=countWhere(sources,λs:cell:indexHit(cells,s,indexChannel,channel,offset,target,relation))
```

## Example

````markdown
---
format: open-rules
title: Index Count example
setter: Example
source: ""
case: ""
library: https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/
status: read
---

```rules
sudoku 9x9
index-count sources ["r1c1","r1c2"] cells ["r1c3","r1c4"] target 7 total 1
```
````

Satisfies the rule: With source digits 1,3 and lookup digits 7,4, only position 1 hits.

Breaks the rule: With source digits 2,3 and the same lookup digits, neither hits.

name: Close Whispers
url: https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/close-whispers.md
kind: close-whispers
parameters:
  line:
    empty_when: edges
    description: The cells in order, for example r1c1-r1c2-r1c3.
    default: Required.
    type: path<cell>
  gap:
    description: The greatest difference allowed between neighbours.
    default: Required.
    type: number
  channel:
    type: Channel
    description: Read printed digits (D) or effective values (V).
    default: D.
  edges:
    type: optional<list<list<cell>>>
    description: Explicit undirected edges of one connected network; each edge lists two different cells.
    default: Absent; use the ordered line.
---

# Close Whispers

Neighbouring digits along the line differ by at most the stated maximum.

These are also called shout-n lines: use `gap n` for the largest permitted difference. Equal neighbours satisfy the rule when the gap is nonnegative. Digits may repeat when other rules allow.

With explicit `edges`, supply one connected network and write `line []` when no ordered list is needed. The window checks include every simple traversal through its junctions.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| line | The cells in order, for example r1c1-r1c2-r1c3. | Required. |
| gap | The greatest difference allowed between neighbours. | Required. |
| channel | Read printed digits (D) or effective values (V). | D. |
| edges | Explicit undirected edges of one connected network; each edge lists two different cells. | Absent; use the ordered line. |

## Maths

Class: **with aggregates**.

The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate.

```text
lineGeometry(line,edges,false) ∧ ∀W∈lineWindows(line,edges,2,false): |W|=2 → |read(W[0],channel)-read(W[1],channel)|<=gap
```

Every drawn edge is compared, including branches and junctions.

## Example

````markdown
---
format: open-rules
title: Close Whispers example
setter: Example
source: ""
case: ""
library: https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/
status: read
---

```rules
sudoku 9x9
close-whispers r1c1-r1c2 gap 2
```
````

Satisfies the rule: r1c1=1, r1c2=3. The neighbours differ by the permitted maximum 2.

Breaks the rule: r1c1=1, r1c2=4. The neighbours differ by 3, exceeding the maximum 2.

# Remainder Cage

The cage total has the stated remainder after division by the modulus. The distinct parameter forbids repeated digits.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| cells | The marked cells, for example r1c1-r1c2-r2c2. | Required. |
| modulus | The divisor used to take remainders. | Required. modulus ≥ 1. |

# Molecules

Electron digits around each atom add up to its stated total. All cells at or below the electron threshold are electrons; higher digits may also be chosen. Touching atoms share the same electron choices.

## Parameters

  ∧ (∀A∈atoms: sum_D(A∩E)=sum)
```

There is one Boolean electron choice per cell shared by every atom touching it. Cells with D(c) ≤ electronMax are electrons. Each atom’s electron digits sum to sum; higher digits may be electrons or not.

# Cage Expressions

Each cage total equals its expression. Letters stand for whole numbers and keep the same value throughout the rule. The distinct parameter gives different letters different values.

## Parameters

The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate.

```text
∃letterValues:list<position>:
  |letterValues|=letterCount({g.expression:g∈cages}) ∧
  (∀g∈cages: defined(g.expression,letterValues) ∧ eval(g.expression,letterValues)=sum_D(g.cells))
  ∧ (distinct → ∀i,j∈[0,|letterValues|): i!=j → letterValues[i]!=letterValues[j])
```

There is a shared assignment of integers to letters such that each evaluated expression equals its cage total. distinct requires different letters to have different values. Division is exact with nonzero divisor; powers require a nonnegative integer exponent.

# Mapped Values

Constrain one numeric channel using a shared selection inside scope. Selected cells use an affine transformation, an explicit digit-to-value map, or a free value from the allowed list. Unselected cells in scope keep their digits. Outside scope, identity requires the face digit and free imposes no condition. Each digit has at most one map entry; every selected digit must have an entry in map mode. Declarations sharing V or any named channel conjoin on the same values, with no constructor uniqueness requirement. All equations must hold together. The default outside free leaves other scopes unconstrained. Named channels are read through channelValue in formulas; the reserved channel V is the effective value used by existing valued rules. Channel D cannot be written.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| selectionRef | Selection name; H means board shading. | Required. |
| scope | Cells where the selected transformation applies. | Required. |
| values | Output channel; V or an independent name. | "V". |
| mode | Transformation of selected digits. | affine. |
| factor | Affine multiplier. | 1. |
| offset | Affine offset. | 0. |
| mapping | Explicit digit and value records. | Empty list. |
| allowed | Allowed selected values in free mode. | Empty list. |
| different | Require selected values to differ from face digits. | false. |
| outside | Policy for cells outside scope. | free. |

## Maths

Class: **existential**.

The [shared predicates](predicates.md) define the notation and operations.

```text
values!="D" ∧ validValueMap(mapping) ∧ ∀c∈C: let v=channelValue(values,c); if c∈scope then (if marked(selectionRef,c) then (if mode="affine" then v=factor*D(c)+offset else if mode="map" then mappedValue(D(c),v,mapping) else v∈allowed) ∧ (different → v!=D(c)) else v=D(c)) else (outside="identity" → v=D(c))
```

# Primality

Prime and composite digits alternate along the line. On a standard board, primes are 2, 3, 5, 7 and composites are 4, 6, 8, 9.

With explicit `edges`, supply one connected network and write `line []` when no ordered list is needed. The window checks include every simple traversal through its junctions.

| line | The cells in order, for example r1c1-r1c2-r1c3. | Required. |

## Maths

Class: **with aggregates**.

The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate.

```text
lineGeometry(line,edges,loop) ∧ (∀c∈line:D(c)>1) ∧ (present(edges) → ∀c∈graphVertices(unwrap(edges)):D(c)>1)
∧ ∀W∈lineWindows(line,edges,2,loop): |W|=2 → ¬(prime(D(W[0]))↔prime(D(W[1])))
```

Every digit is greater than one. Neighbouring path positions alternate prime and composite digits. Include last/first when loop is true.

# Rule-line syntax

A case file declares its library root once. Every rule name resolves to its Markdown definition under that root.
One line states a rule, its cells and parameters, with an optional condition.
The [declaration grammar](../spec/declarations.ebnf) defines the complete syntax.

```ebnf
instance = [id ":" space] *("not" space) rule [space condition]
rule = reference [space cells] (keyword-parameters | named-parameters)
named-parameters = *(space parameter space value)
keyword-parameters = space declared-keyword *(space declared-operand) named-parameters
condition = ("if" | "unless") space predicate
predicate = "uniform" | "distinct" | "connected"
reference = kind-name | section-fragment | HTTPS-Markdown-URL
cells = cell *("-" cell | "," cell)
cell = "r" positive-row "c" positive-column
value = JSON-value | cell
```

The instance ID precedes every operator. An unquoted ID starts with a Unicode letter or ASCII digit and continues with letters, combining marks, ASCII digits, underscores, hyphens or dots: `clue-1:`, `2nd-clue:`, `group.a:`. Quote reserved declaration words (`not`, `if`, `unless`, `true`, `false`, `null`, `uniform`, `distinct`, `connected`), cell or path spellings, dimensions and numbers: `"r1c1":`, `"9x9":`, `"12":`. Other characters and whitespace also require JSON quotes. Repeated kinds need distinct IDs, including a positive and negated instance of the same kind.
The `total` parameter aliases cage `sum`; the writer uses `total`.
A separate `#` followed by whitespace or the end of the line starts a comment.
A fragment such as `#weighted-triple` remains a rule reference.
The cell path lists each cell explicitly; r1c1-r1c3 names two cells, not a three-cell range.

## Custom definitions and boards

A case may define a custom rule inside its own file. A declaration such as
`weighted_1: #weighted-triple r1c1-r1c2-r1c3` references an embedded definition with `id: weighted-triple`. The id is scoped
to this file and is independent of headings. A setter-chosen external
HTTPS Markdown URL is also allowed. The definition has `id` and/or `url`, `name`, `parameters`,
`definition`, `maths` and `example`; every definition is referenced. See the
[case-file contract](../spec/case-files.md) for the full layout and checks.

On non-standard dimensions or alphabets, state board-dependent parameters
explicitly, including whispers `loop`, cage `repeats` and sandwich `crusts`.
The case-file contract lists all such parameters, board fields and given forms.

## Pair relationships and Kropki

The parameter declarations on [pair](pair.md) define its keyword grammar. Write two cells, the relationship keyword, then a whole-number value where needed:

```rules
pair_1: pair r1c1-r1c2 ratio 3
pair_2: pair r4c4-r4c5 difference 2
pair_3: pair r2c2-r3c2 sum 10
pair_4: pair r5c1-r5c2 at-least 4
pair_5: pair r6c1-r6c2 less
pair_6: pair r7c1-r7c2 multiple
pair_7: pair r8c1-r8c2 shift
```

`less`, `multiple` and `shift` take no value. `less` preserves the cells' order. The page defines each relationship. Pair lines no longer use a `relation` JSON object.

[Kropki](kropki.md) is shorthand: `kropki r1c1-r1c2 white` means `pair r1c1-r1c2 difference 1`; `kropki r1c1-r1c2 black` means `pair r1c1-r1c2 ratio 2`. The existing named forms `colour "white"` and `colour "black"` are accepted too. These names state relationships; the dot's painted colour is drawing metadata. Use pair for ratio 3, difference n, sum n, grey or brown dots, and other relationships.

### Declaring keyword syntax

A typed parameter may opt into `syntax: {form: cells, count: 2}` for its primary cell list. Its companion parameter declares `form: keywords`, a `tag` naming a record's enum field, and `choices` mapping every enum member to an ordered mapping of operand fields and their line types. For pair, `ratio: {value: integer}` builds `{op: "ratio", value: 3}` from `ratio 3`; `less: {}` builds `{op: "less"}`. Integer operands are kept exactly, without floating-point rounding. This line notation does not narrow the formula's numeric domain.

A plain enum uses keyword choices without a tag. `named: true` also accepts the parameter name followed by its keyword or quoted keyword; Kropki uses this to preserve existing case files. Declarations must match their parameter types. This grammar applies by declaration to any kind; no kind names or operation names are built into the parser.

## Negation and conditions

`not` negates the entire base rule formula, including its internal quantifiers.
Two `not` prefixes cancel; they remain recorded for writing.
A trailing condition wraps that base formula after its negations.
For S, the rule's own cell list, and R, its fully instantiated meaning:

```math
Meaning(not R) ↔ ¬R
Meaning(R if P) ↔ P(S) → R
Meaning(R unless P) ↔ ¬P(S) → R
Meaning(not R unless P) ↔ ¬P(S) → ¬R
```

The condition applies the named shared predicate to that rule's cells; it takes no independent cell argument.
A rule without a nonempty primary cell list cannot carry a condition.
Only one trailing condition is allowed. The condition keywords uniform and connected call the corresponding shared unary Boolean terms on a cell set. The distinct condition uses distinct_D for a cell set and distinctAt with D for an ordered list, comparing different positions. Unknown predicates and terms needing additional arguments are errors.
Invalid parameters, missing definitions and off-board cells remain errors under negation or an inactive condition.

`uniform` reads the single shared shading answer declared by `yin-yang`.
It means all the clue's cells are shaded or all are unshaded.
`unless uniform` means the clue contains both shades.
The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define its formula and the answer binding.

```rules
yin-yang
cage_1: cage r1c2-r1c3 total 17 repeats true if uniform
cage_2: not cage r1c2-r1c3 total 17 repeats true unless uniform
renban r1c5-r1c6-r1c7 if uniform
nabner r1c5-r1c6-r1c7 distinct true unless uniform
quadruple r5c3-r5c4-r6c3-r6c4 digits [2,9] if uniform
absent-digits r5c3-r5c4-r6c3-r6c4 digits [2,9] unless uniform
```

The cage's `repeats true` leaves only the sum condition to negate.
Nabner explicitly requires different digits in this example.
These are syntax examples, not the full Yin Yagn clue list.

Mixed Renban clues can require Nabner; ¬renban alone also permits nonconsecutive sets that fail Nabner.
A mixed quadruple requiring no listed digit uses `absent-digits`.
Negating quadruple only requires that its complete list is not present; some listed digits may still appear.
WROGN is setter wording with explicit meanings, not a library kind or an automatic negation mapping.

## Global rules and shared answers

Negation is defined for a global rule when its complete formula is defined.
For example, `not anti-king` requires at least one equal king-related pair.
A global reference with no definition cannot be negated.
`not sudoku 9x9` negates the row-column-box composition once, rather than negating each house.
It still declares the board's dimensions, alphabet and standard boxes.

Shading belongs to the shared case answer. Its existential binding stays outside the conjunction of rules.
Other witnesses keep the binders in their owning rule formulas; value-modifier binds M inside its formula.
A negated Yin Yang formula is checked on that supplied shading, not on a separate shading chosen by a clue.

```math
CaseMeaning(D) ↔ ∃H ⊆ C: ∧_{r∈DeclaredRules} Meaning(r,D,H)
```

## Every rule negated

Case front matter `negate: all` wraps each declared base rule once, before its condition is applied.
An explicit `not` cancels this extra negation for that instance.
It negates each rule individually, not the conjunction of rules.
Sudoku remains one composed rule even though exchange expands its houses.
Board data, givens, definitions and drawings are not predicates to negate.

## Typed composition

These checked definitions operate on instantiated rule meanings. Every instance reads the same face/value channels and shared shading. Witnesses bound inside a rule, including the modifier set M, stay inside that rule when it is negated.

```openrules
term negateRule(base:boolean):boolean = ¬base;
term conditionalRule(base:boolean,condition:boolean):boolean = condition → base;
term unlessRule(base:boolean,condition:boolean):boolean = ¬condition → base;
term negatedUnlessRule(base:boolean,condition:boolean):boolean = ¬condition → ¬base;
term composeRules(instantiated:list<boolean>):boolean = ∀meaning∈instantiated: meaning;
```

## Decorative marks

Declare markings as decoration only when the puzzle text explicitly says they
carry no rule. List their cells, including every cell of a region:

```rules
decoration r1c1-r1c2-r2c2 note "Ignore the grey ribbon." element "grey-ribbon"
```

[Decoration](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/decoration.md) adds no condition.
The optional `element` metadata is available on every declaration and identifies
the same drawn mark across declarations. Sharing cells alone does not identify
the same mark. Do not use negation or conditions on decoration.

# Line Choice

The line satisfies between the stated minimum and maximum number of the listed line rules.

With explicit `edges`, supply one connected network and write `line []` when no ordered list is needed. The window checks include every simple traversal through its junctions.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| line | The cells in order, for example r1c1-r1c2-r1c3. | Required. |
| kinds | The line rules available to choose from. | Required. |
| min | The least number of listed rules that must hold. | Required. |
| max | The greatest number of listed rules or different digits allowed. | Required. |
| loop | Whether the line closes, joining its last cell back to its first. | false (open path). |
| edges | Explicit undirected edges of one connected network; each edge lists two different cells. | Absent; use the ordered line. |

## Maths

Class: **with aggregates**.

The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate.

```text
lineGeometry(line,edges,loop) ∧ let S=if present(edges) then graphVertices(unwrap(edges)) else {c∈C:c∈line};
let selected=λoption:enum{renban,nabner,modular,entropic,parity}:
  (option="renban" ∧ (if present(edges) then consecutiveValues(S,"D",false) else consecutiveValues(line,"D",false)))
  ∨ (option="nabner" ∧ (if present(edges) then nonconsecutiveValues(S,"D",true,false) else nonconsecutiveValues(line,"D",true,false)))
  ∨ (option="modular" ∧ (if present(edges) then modularMeaning(line,edges,loop,3,3) else ∀W∈lineWindows(line,edges,3,loop): distinctAt(W,λc:cell:classMod3(D(c)))))
  ∨ (option="entropic" ∧ (if present(edges) then entropicMeaning(line,edges,loop) else |𝔄|>0 ∧ |𝔄| mod 3=0 ∧ ∀W∈lineWindows(line,edges,3,loop): distinctAt(W,λc:cell:classEntropy(D(c)))))
  ∨ (option="parity" ∧ parityMeaning(line,edges,loop));
min<=countWhere(kinds,selected)<=max
```

Renban reads D; Nabner reads D and permits repeats. Ordered modular and entropic choices check three-position windows, so an open two-cell choice is vacuous. Explicit networks use the standalone component checks, including distinct classes when the component is smaller than the window. Negation applies to this entire counted choice.

# Maze

A tree has no cycle and gives a unique route between each pair of vertices. With tree false, cycles are allowed. A one-cell tree has no edges and no degree-one leaves.

# Equality Cage

Cage digits are different. The number of low odd digits equals the number of high even digits; low even and high odd counts also match.

## Parameters

```text
distinct_D(cells) ∧ (∀c∈cells: D(c)!=(|𝔄|+1)/2)
∧ countWhere(cells,λc:cell: D(c)<(|𝔄|+1)/2 ∧ odd(D(c)))=countWhere(cells,λc:cell: D(c)>(|𝔄|+1)/2 ∧ ¬odd(D(c)))
∧ countWhere(cells,λc:cell: D(c)<(|𝔄|+1)/2 ∧ ¬odd(D(c)))=countWhere(cells,λc:cell: D(c)>(|𝔄|+1)/2 ∧ odd(D(c)))

# Hidden Modular

Choose the span by its stated extent. Every three consecutive digits in that span have different remainders when divided by 3.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| cells | The marked cells, for example r1c1-r1c2-r2c2. | Required. |
| extent | How to choose the span: to-max, between-ends or first-x. | Required. |

## Maths

Class: **with aggregates**.

The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate.

```text
|𝔄|>0 ∧ ∃a,b∈[0,|cells|):
  a<=b ∧ ((extent="to-max" ∧ a=0 ∧ firstOccurrence(cells,𝔄[|𝔄|-1],b))
    ∨ (extent="between-ends" ∧ ∃i,j∈[0,|cells|): firstOccurrence(cells,𝔄[0],i)
       ∧ firstOccurrence(cells,𝔄[|𝔄|-1],j) ∧ a=minimumPosition(i,j) ∧ b=maximumPosition(i,j))
    ∨ (extent="first-x" ∧ a=0 ∧ |cells|>0 ∧ 1<=D(cells[0])<=|cells| ∧ b=D(cells[0])-1))
  ∧ ∀s∈[a,b-1): distinctAt(window(cells,3,s,false),λc:cell: classMod3(D(c)))
```

Choose the span from the clue through the maximum (to-max), between minimum and maximum inclusive (between-ends), or the first D(cells[0]) positions (first-x). Every triple in that span has three distinct remainders modulo 3.

    description: Require this many marker occurrences in every region.
    default: Absent; no marker count condition.
  rays:
    type: list<record{cells:list<cell>,total:position}>

    default: Empty list.

# Region Clue

Each marker compares its region aggregate with target when supplied. Without target, it uses the marker’s own number in channel (D by default), including when operation is count. Repeated markers count as separate occurrences for per-region counts. A crossing clue counts consecutive pairs belonging to different regions of this shared partition; every ray cell must belong to the partition. Returning to a previously visited region counts another boundary crossing.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| partitionRef | The shared region collection name. | Required. |
| markers | Cells whose containing region is constrained. | Required. |
| operation | Aggregate over each containing region. | sum. |
| target | Fixed aggregate target. | Absent; read the marker number. |
| channel | Read printed digits (D) or effective values (V). | D. |
| perRegion | Require this many marker occurrences in every region. | Absent; no marker count condition. |
| rays | Ordered rays and their required count of changes between regions. | Empty list. |

## Maths

Class: **existential**.

The [shared predicates](predicates.md) define the notation and operations.

```text
let P=partitionAnswer(partitionRef); |P|>0 ∧ (∀m∈markers: ∃R∈P: m∈R ∧ aggregate(R,channel,operation)=(if present(target) then unwrap(target) else read(m,channel))) ∧ (present(perRegion) → ∀R∈P:countWhere(markers,λm:cell:m∈R)=unwrap(perRegion)) ∧ (∀g∈rays: (∀c∈g.cells:∃R∈P:c∈R) ∧ g.total=(count i∈[0,|g.cells|-1): ¬samePartition(P,g.cells[i],g.cells[i+1])))
```

# Pair

The two values obey the stated relationship: a difference, ratio, total, multiple, inequality or shift.

X clues use `sum 10`; V clues use `sum 5`. A numbered white dot uses `difference n`, and a numbered black dot uses `ratio n`. An unnumbered white or black dot uses 1 or 2 respectively, as defined by [Kropki](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/kropki.md). These positive clues do not imply that every possible clue is drawn; use [Negative](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/negative.md) for that condition.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| relation | The relationship keyword and any required whole-number value, for example difference 1. | Required. |
| cells | The two marked cells in order, for example r1c1-r1c2. | Required. |
| channel | Read printed digits (D) or effective values (V). | V. |

## Rule lines

Write the two cells in order, then a relationship keyword. Values in rule lines are whole numbers. The `relation` parameter declares these keyword forms; tools derive the grammar from that declaration.

| Form | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `pair r1c1-r1c2 difference 2` | The values differ by exactly 2. |
| `pair r1c1-r1c2 at-least 3` | The values differ by at least 3. |
| `pair r1c1-r1c2 ratio 3` | One value is three times the other. |
| `pair r1c1-r1c2 sum 10` | The values total 10. |
| `pair r1c1-r1c2 less` | The first value is less than the second. |
| `pair r1c1-r1c2 multiple` | The larger is an integer multiple of the smaller; two zeros also satisfy it. |
| `pair r1c1-r1c2 shift` | Both values are integers other than 5; they share exactly one of parity and being greater than 5. |

A dot's colour is drawing metadata. State its relationship with `pair`, whether the dot is grey, brown or another colour. [Kropki](kropki.md) names the two usual relationships: white is `difference 1`, black is `ratio 2`. The former `relation {"op":...}` form is replaced by these keywords.

## Maths

Class: **first-order**.

The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate.

```text
|cells|=2 ∧ pairRelation(relation,read(cells[0],channel),read(cells[1],channel))
```

The shared pair relation compares the selected channel.

# Nabner

No two marked numbers are one apart. `distinct true` also forbids equal numbers; repeats are allowed by default. The default channel reads printed digits.

The rule applies to the whole cell set or connected network component, including every branch. `channel "V"` reads effective values. With fractional values, `separated true` requires every pair to differ by more than one.

With `selection`, apply the rule to a stopping prefix of the ordered line. The prefix ends at the first target number, given or listed crust digit. `include` controls whether that cell is kept. A stopping cell must exist. Prefix selection uses the stated channel and an ordered line.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| selection | A stopping prefix, with its target or crust digits and inclusion policy. | Absent; use the whole cell set or network. |
| line | All cells of the line or cell set; order does not affect comparisons. | Required. |
| distinct | Whether repeated digits are forbidden. | false (repeats allowed). |
| edges | Explicit undirected edges of one connected network; each edge lists two different cells. | Absent; use the ordered line. |
| channel | Read printed digits (D) or effective values (V). | D. |
| separated | Require a difference greater than one instead of merely forbidding a difference of one. | false. |

## Maths

Class: **with aggregates**.

The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate.

else lineGeometry(line,edges,false) ∧ (if present(edges) then nonconsecutiveValues(graphVertices(unwrap(edges)),channel,¬distinct,separated) else nonconsecutiveValues(line,channel,¬distinct,separated))
```

Every pair in the whole cell set or network component is compared. distinct controls repeats. separated distinguishes a strict gap greater than one on fractional effective values.

# Route Group

Relate at least two distinct named routes. They may be disjoint, separated by a chosen move, free from proper interior step crossings, or together cover a cell set. Each route receives its topology from a Route declaration using the same name. The group reads each route’s closure separately, so open routes and closed loops can share a group.

A long step passing through a visited cell is allowed by `crossings false` when that cell is an endpoint of the other step. Only intersections strictly inside both steps count; collinear overlaps do not count.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| routes | Shared route names, each listed once. | Required. |
| disjoint | Require different routes to share no cells. | true. |
| noTouch | Forbid this move between cells of different routes. | Absent; no extra separation. |
| crossings | Allow crossings between straight steps of any length of different routes. | false. |
| cover | Require the union of routes to equal this cell set. | Absent; no covering condition. |

## Maths

Class: **existential**.

The [shared predicates](predicates.md) define the notation and operations.

```text
|routes|>=2 ∧ (∀n∈routes: |routeAnswer(n)|>0) ∧ (∀i,j∈[0,|routes|): i!=j → routes[i]!=routes[j]) ∧ (∀i,j∈[0,|routes|): i<j → let L=routeAnswer(routes[i]); let M=routeAnswer(routes[j]); (disjoint → ∀c∈L:c∉M) ∧ (present(noTouch) → ∀a∈L: ∀b∈M: ¬moveRelation(unwrap(noTouch),a,b)) ∧ (crossings ∨ ¬routeCrosses(L,M,routeClosed(routes[i]),routeClosed(routes[j])))) ∧ (present(cover) → {c∈C:∃n∈routes:c∈routeAnswer(n)}=unwrap(cover))
```

Each region must match an allowed template when templates are supplied. Template counts count each match, so congruent templates describe the same matching class. Every window of consecutive cells has different remainders modulo the stated modulus. The window length defaults to three and is independent of the modulus. An open two-cell line has different remainders.

With explicit edges, every simple traversal of the stated length is checked, including every turn through a junction. A cell is not revisited within a window. With an ordered line, loop windows cross the last-to-first join.

With explicit `edges`, supply one connected network and write `line []` when no ordered list is needed. The window checks include every simple traversal through its junctions.

# Shifter Line

Digits on the line cannot be 5. Within a region, neighbours are both odd or both even and both below or both above 5. At each region crossing, exactly one of those relationships changes.

With explicit `edges`, every edge in the connected network follows the same region-crossing rule. Write `line []` when no ordered list is needed.

| --- | --- | --- |

∧ ∀W∈lineWindows(line,edges,2,false): |W|=2 →
  let P=(odd(D(W[0]))↔odd(D(W[1]))); let Q=(high(D(W[0]))↔high(D(W[1])));

Numeric edge relations follow increasing board cell order, so directed relations have a fixed orientation. A Maze declaration supplies connectivity and vertex scope. A one-cell network has no edges and may satisfy this clue.

# Difference Line

Same difference means every drawn edge has the same absolute difference. Different difference means every distinct drawn edge has a different absolute difference. Signed step means one signed step repeats along the ordered line.

A network is undirected. Signed steps use the supplied line order and do not accept network edges. Reversing a line reverses its signed step. Diamond clues apply only to same difference.

With explicit `edges`, supply one connected network and write `line []` when no ordered list is needed. The window checks include every simple traversal through its junctions.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| line | The ordered line; supply an empty list when edges describe a network. | Required. |
| edges | Explicit undirected edges of one connected network; each edge lists two different cells. | Absent; use the ordered line. |
| loop | Include the last-to-first edge. | false. |
| mode | Equal absolute differences, distinct absolute differences, or a signed arithmetic progression. | Required. |
| channel | Read printed digits (D) or effective values (V). | D. |
| diamonds | Clue cells equal to the common absolute difference. | Empty set. |

## Maths

Class: **with aggregates**.

The [shared predicates](predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate.

```text

∧ (mode!="signed-step" → (∀p,q∈W: |p|=2 ∧ |q|=2 → ((mode="same" → |read(p[0],channel)-read(p[1],channel)|=|read(q[0],channel)-read(q[1],channel)|) ∧ (mode="different" ∧ {p[0],p[1]}!={q[0],q[1]} → |read(p[0],channel)-read(p[1],channel)|!=|read(q[0],channel)-read(q[1],channel)|))) ∧ (mode="different" → |diamonds|=0) ∧ (mode="same" → ∀g∈diamonds: ∀p∈W: |p|=2 → read(g,channel)=|read(p[0],channel)-read(p[1],channel)|))
```

# Derived Count

Derive one number from every operand pair, then count matching occurrences, distinct results, or rank a target among those results. Rank is one plus the number of occurrences strictly below the target; ties share that rank. Ratios divide left by right and require a nonzero right result. Distinct mode removes equal results only after every quantity has been calculated.

In distinct mode, omit target and relation.

| quantities | Ordered aggregate pairs and their sum, product, absolute difference or directed ratio. | Required. |

| target | Comparison target; unused in distinct mode. | 0. |
| relation | Relation from each result to the target in matches mode. | difference 0 (equal). |
| total | Required count or rank. | Required. |

## Maths

Class: **with aggregates**.

The [shared predicates](predicates.md) define the notation and operations.

```text
(∀q∈quantities: quantityValid(q)) ∧ (if mode="distinct" then total=|{quantity(q):q∈{x∈quantities:quantityValid(x)}}| else if mode="rank" then total=1+countWhere(quantities,λq:DerivedQuantity:quantityValid(q) ∧ quantity(q)<target) else total=countWhere(quantities,λq:DerivedQuantity:quantityValid(q) ∧ pairRelation(relation,quantity(q),target)))

# Cell Entries

Give every cell in scope a list of symbols from the board alphabet, with the stated size bounds and repeat policy. The names `D` and `V` are reserved for face digits and effective values and cannot be written. These are additional solution entries, read through symbolAnswer(name,c); they do not replace D. Optionally equate D to their sum or first entry. First-entry mode requires a nonempty list even when minimum is zero. Lists preserve order and repeated symbols; cells outside scope are unconstrained by this declaration.

| faceMode | Relationship to the face digit D. | independent. |

The [shared predicates](predicates.md) define the notation and operations.

```text

# Paired Roles

Pair each cell in the left role with exactly one cell in the right role, covering scope. The roles are disjoint shared selections with different names. Network edges are undirected; the numeric relation always reads the left-role cell first and the right-role cell second. Empty roles and an empty pairing are allowed only for empty scope.

| left | Left selection name. | Required. |
| right | Right selection name. | Required. |

| relation | Numeric relation from left to right. | Required. |
| channel | Read face digits D or effective values V. | D. |

Class: **existential**.

The [shared predicates](predicates.md) define the notation and operations.

```text
left!=right ∧ let A=selectedCells(left); let B=selectedCells(right); let E=networkAnswer(name); A∪B=scope ∧ |A∩B|=0 ∧ canonicalEdges(E) ∧ (∀e∈E:|e|=2 ∧ ((e[0]∈A ∧ e[1]∈B) ∨ (e[1]∈A ∧ e[0]∈B))) ∧ (∀a∈A:∀b∈B:graphEdge(E,a,b) → pairRelation(relation,read(a,channel),read(b,channel))) ∧ (∀c∈scope:networkDegree(E,c)=1)

# Region Sum

Region boundaries split the line into segments. By default, each segment has the same total value. With combine true, all visits to a region contribute to one total, equal across the regions visited.

The board’s primary regions supply the boundaries: standard boxes on a normal Sudoku board, or the declared regions on an irregular board. List the maximal runs in `segments` in path order, including every return to a region. `combine false` keeps those visits separate; `combine true` adds their values together within each region. State the choice explicitly when a line re-enters a region. Digits may repeat when other rules allow; each occurrence on the supplied path contributes to its sum.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| combine | Whether separate visits to the same region contribute to one regional total. | false (each visit is summed separately). |
| line | The cells in order, for example r1c1-r1c2-r1c3. | Required. |
| segments | The cells in each segment, listed in path order. | Required. |
| channel | Read printed digits (D) or effective values (V). | V. |

## Maths

Class: **with aggregates**.

The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate.

```text
maximalRegionRuns(line,segments) ∧ if combine then
  ∀R,S∈Regions: (∃c∈line:c∈R) ∧ (∃c∈line:c∈S) → aggregate(⟨c:c∈line,c∈R⟩,channel,"sum")=aggregate(⟨c:c∈line,c∈S⟩,channel,"sum")
else ∀A,B∈segments: aggregate(A,channel,"sum")=aggregate(B,channel,"sum")
```

Segments must be exactly the ordered maximal primary-region runs, retaining every path occurrence. The selected channel is summed per visit or per visited region.

```
````

Breaks the rule: r1c2=1, r1c3=2, r1c4=4. The listed segments have totals 3 and 4.

### Returning to a region

```rules

```

Satisfies the rule: r1c3=1, r1c4=3, r2c3=2. The first box contributes 1+2 and the second contributes 3. Breaks the rule: r1c3=1, r1c4=4, r2c3=2 gives totals 3 and 4. With combine false, [3,3,3] satisfies the three separate segment sums but fails the combined totals of 6 and 3.

# Layered Cage

Each occupied row of the cage contains only upper digits or only other digits. Every upper row is above every other row.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| cells | The marked cells, for example r1c1-r1c2-r2c2. | Required. |
| upper | The digits treated as the upper layer. | Required. |

## Maths

Class: **first-order**.

The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate.

```text
∀a,b ∈ cells:
  (row(a)=row(b) → ((D(a)∈upper) ↔ (D(b)∈upper)))
  ∧ (D(a)∈upper ∧ D(b)∉upper → row(a)<row(b))
```

Each occupied row of cells contains only upper digits or only non-upper digits. Every upper row precedes every non-upper row from top to bottom. Sums and distinctness belong to a separate cage rule.

Breaks the rule: r1c1=1, r2c1=2. The upper digit is below the other layer.

# Symbol House

Each supplied house has exactly the stated multiplicity of each listed symbol across all entries of its cells in a shared symbol channel. No other symbol is allowed there. Zero counts express missing symbols; counts above one express repeated symbols. Houses are sets of cells; multiple entries within a cell count separately. The default name `D` counts the face digits, once per cell. Use Cell Entries to set the per-cell symbol domain and relationship to D.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| symbols | Symbol channel name; D reads one face digit per cell. | "D". |
| houses | Groups whose symbol multiplicities are constrained. | Required. |
| digits | Distinct symbols to count. | Required. |
| counts | Exact counts in the same order as digits. | Required. |

## Maths

Class: **existential**.

The [shared predicates](predicates.md) define the notation and operations.

```text
|digits|=|counts| ∧ distinctAt(digits,λd:digit:d) ∧ (∀d∈digits:d∈𝔄) ∧ (∀n∈counts:n>=0) ∧ ∀G∈houses: (∀c∈G:∀d∈cellSymbols(symbols,c):d∈digits) ∧ (∀i∈[0,|digits|): 0<=i ∧ i<|counts| ∧ (Σ_{c∈G}countWhere(cellSymbols(symbols,c),λd:digit:d=digits[i]))=counts[i])
```

# Bremban

The distinct digits in the marked cells form a consecutive run, in any order. Digits may repeat where the other rules allow it. This is Renban without its no-repeat condition.

The marked cells can also be a cage. Declare its sum separately with [Cage](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/cage.md), using `repeats true` when repetitions are allowed.

## Parameters

| --- | --- | --- |
| edges | Explicit connected network. | Absent; use the listed cells. |
| selection | A stopping prefix. | Absent; use the whole cell set. |
| line | The marked cells; order does not affect the consecutive set. | Required. |

## Maths

The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate.

Bremban binds [Renban](renban.md) to printed digits with repeats allowed. Its header supplies the canonical parameters.

The distinct printed digits form one consecutive run; repeats are allowed.

# Choice Count

Count true labels in one shared Boolean assignment. Names must be distinct, so a repeated label cannot create an extra vote. Reify each label against the complete intended rule meaning in a formula using reified(choiceAnswer("label"),meaning). For a liar this is equivalence to the truthful meaning; a false label requires that entire meaning to fail. An explicitly inverted rule uses conditionalMeaning with its separately stated true and false meanings.

Each marked digit gives a position along its row or column. The cell at that position contains the marked cell’s column number for column indexing, or row number for row indexing.

# Aggregate Relation

Select the cells of each operand, calculate its result, and compare the two results. An operand can sum, multiply, count, or read a decimal number. Each operand states its digit or value channel and whether numbers may repeat.

List cells in reading order. Optional zero-based `start` and `length` select a slice; omitted values select the whole list. A list retains every occurrence, even when it names a cell more than once. Optional `stop` then selects a prefix ending at the first target number, given or listed crust digit. That stopping cell is excluded unless `include` is true. The stopping cell must exist. Decimal reading uses D and requires each printed symbol to be a digit from 0 to 9.

The familiar [Cage](cage.md), [Little Killer](little-killer.md), [Arrow](arrow.md), [Double Arrow](double-arrow.md), [Equal Sums](equal-sums.md) and [Region Sum](region-sum.md) use the same shared aggregate operations with their own operand selection and defaults.

This is [Aggregate Equation](aggregate-equation.md) with one term on each side, each term using the corresponding operand with coefficient 1 and power 1, sum on both sides, and the same relation. Aggregate Equation owns the general equation meaning.

# Entropic

On a standard 1–9 board, every three consecutive cells on the path contain one low digit (1–3), one middle digit (4–6) and one high digit (7–9), in any order. On a two-cell open path, the digits come from different groups.

For other boards, divide the puzzle’s ordered list of allowed symbols into three equal-sized groups. This list is called the ordered alphabet. The groups follow its supplied order, not necessarily numerical order; its length must be divisible by three. On a loop, triples also cross the join between the last and first cells.

For an ordered alphabet of 1–6, the three groups are 1–2, 3–4 and 5–6. Digits may repeat more than two positions apart when other rules allow.

With explicit `edges`, supply one connected network and write `line []` when no ordered list is needed. The window checks include every simple traversal through its junctions.

# Digit Profile

Each listed class occurs its stated number of times. Overlapping classes count independently. Repeating a number inside a class does not count it twice. Repeated cell occurrences count separately. # Sandwich

The clue gives the sum of digits strictly between the two crusts, counted from the clue side. State the crust digits and their occurrence policy.

On a standard 1–9 board the usual crusts are 1 and 9. The crust digits are excluded from the sum; adjacent crusts give a total of zero. List the row or column from the clue side.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| cells | The marked cells, for example r1c1-r1c2-r2c2. | Required. |
| sum | The total the digits or values must add up to. | Required. |
| endpointOccurrences | Whether both endpoints must occur exactly once or at most once. | No extra occurrence condition. |
| crusts | The two crust digits that bound the sandwich. | Lowest and highest board symbols. |

## Maths

Class: **with aggregates**.

The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate.

```text
|𝔄|>0 ∧ (if present(crusts) then
  ∀i,j∈{t∈[0,|cells|):D(cells[t])∈unwrap(crusts)}: i<j ∧ ¬(∃k∈{t∈[0,|cells|):D(cells[t])∈unwrap(crusts)}:k<j ∧ k!=i) → sum_D(betweenPositions(cells,i,j))=sum
else let lo=𝔄[0]; let hi=𝔄[|𝔄|-1];
  (∀i,j∈[0,|cells|): firstOccurrence(cells,lo,i) ∧ firstOccurrence(cells,hi,j) → sum_D(betweenPositions(cells,i,j))=sum)
  ∧ (endpointOccurrences="exactly-one" → countWhere(cells,λc:cell:D(c)=lo)=1 ∧ countWhere(cells,λc:cell:D(c)=hi)=1)
  ∧ (endpointOccurrences="at-most-one" → countWhere(cells,λc:cell:D(c)=lo)<=1 ∧ countWhere(cells,λc:cell:D(c)=hi)<=1))
```

For custom crusts, sum digits strictly between the first two crust occurrences from the clue. Otherwise use the first lowest/highest symbols and require the between-sum only when both occur. exactly-one requires both once; at-most-one forbids repeated endpoints but allows missing endpoints.

# Arrow

An arrow’s shaft sums to its bulb. Complete one-cell arrows compare effective values (printed digits after declared value modifiers) on both sides; every other case compares printed digits. A bulb with several cells forms a decimal number from its printed digits, in the supplied order. Digits may repeat on complete and partial arrows unless another puzzle rule forbids it.

For an ordinary horizontal bulb, list its cells left to right; for a vertical bulb, list them top to bottom. The supplied order determines the number, including for an unusually shaped bulb.

`partial true` means the supplied shaft is incomplete, for example because fog hides at least one more shaft cell. It does not mean that some player entries are blank. The visible shaft’s printed digits must leave a sum that a non-empty sequence of allowed digits can supply. On a standard 1–9 board, the visible sum is strictly less than the bulb number. If zero is allowed, equality is possible because the omitted part can contain zero.

When several shafts leave the same bulb, declare each shaft separately with the same `bulb` list. Each shaft must reach the bulb total on its own; their sums are not combined. The `line` lists shaft cells only, excluding the bulb.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| partial | Whether the declaration supplies only a shaft fragment, for example under fog. | false (complete arrow). |
| bulb | The bulb cells in decimal reading order, normally left to right or top to bottom. | Required. |
| line | The shaft cells in order, for example r1c1-r1c2-r1c3. | Required. |

## Maths

Class: **existential**.

The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate.

```text
|bulb|>0 ∧ (|bulb|>1 → decimalValid(bulb)) ∧ let B=if |bulb|=1 then D(bulb[0]) else if decimalValid(bulb) then decimal(bulb) else 0;
(partial → ∃remainder:list<digit>: |remainder|>0 ∧ (∀d∈remainder:d∈𝔄) ∧ aggregate(line,"D","sum")+Σ_{d∈remainder}d=B)
∧ (¬partial → (|bulb|=1 → aggregate(line,"V","sum")=V(bulb[0])) ∧ (|bulb|!=1 → aggregate(line,"D","sum")=B))
```

The shared decimal reading forms the bulb. Complete one-cell arrows use V on both sides; all other arrows use D. A partial shaft leaves a nonempty arithmetic remainder from the allowed alphabet.

# Fog

Part of the grid is covered. Only the lit cells are shown, and entering the right digits lights more of them. Fog is a setup feature of the puzzle, declared in the case-file header, and not a rule line. It defines which cells are visible.

## Case-file header

```yaml
fog:
  initiallyLit: [r2c1, r2c2]      # cells clear at the start; [] for a fully covered grid
  links:                          # absent: neighbourhood reveal. Present, even []: links only
    - trigger: [r1c2]             # every cell here must hold a correct entry
      lights: [r2c3, r2c4, r2c5]  # cells lit when the link fires
```

Cells use `r1c1`, like every cell field in the format. Readers also accept 0-based row-major numbers when the board size is known. `lights` and `initiallyLit` cells are on the grid. `trigger` coordinates may lie off it. `links: []` and a missing `links` mean different things, so the key stays when the list is empty.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| initiallyLit | The cells clear at the start; [] for a fully covered grid. | [] (no cell clear at the start). |
| links | The setter's links, each a trigger set and a set of cells it lights. Absent means neighbourhood reveal; present, even [], means links only. | Absent; neighbourhood reveal. |

## Maths

Class: **first-order**.

The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate, including the entries E, placed, correct and visible. Fog gives visible its definition. A cell is lit when it is visible. L₀ is initiallyLit. A Spot is a coordinate that may lie off the board; a link's trigger is a set of spots, so a trigger off the board is expressible and never correct.

```openrules
type Spot = record{row:position,col:position};
type FogLink = record{trigger:set<Spot>,lights:set<cell>};
play term near(a:cell,b:cell):boolean = |row(a)-row(b)|<=1 ∧ |col(a)-col(b)|<=1;
play term correctAt(p:Spot):boolean = ∃c∈C: row(c)=p.row ∧ col(c)=p.col ∧ correct(c);
play term fires(k:FogLink):boolean = ∀t∈k.trigger: correctAt(t);
```

```text
∀c∈C: visible(c) ↔ (c∈initiallyLit ∨
  (if present(links)
   then ∃k∈unwrap(links): c∈k.lights ∧ fires(k)
   else (given(c) ∧ correct(c)) ∨ ∃a∈C: ¬given(a) ∧ correct(a) ∧ near(a,c)))
```

A cell is visible when it is in L₀, or, with links, when a link that lights it has every trigger cell correct, or, without links, when it is a given typed over with its own digit or lies within one row and one column of a correct non-given entry. The right-hand side does not use visible, so visibility depends on the current entries only and is not a fixed point: lighting a cell fires nothing by itself. A trigger need not be visible, a coordinate off the board is never correct, and erasing an entry hides again what only it showed. An empty trigger is an error, so every link has a trigger.

The solution has r1c2=3, r2c2=7, r3c3=4. Lit cells for each set of entries:

- No entries: r1c1, r1c2.
- r1c2=3: r1c1, r1c2, r2c1, r2c2. The first link fires.
- r1c2=3, r2c2=7: the same four cells. The second link needs r3c3 too.
- r1c2=3, r2c2=7, r3c3=4: the four cells and r5c5. Both links fire.
- r1c2=3, r2c2=7, r3c3=5: the four cells. 5 is not the digit, so the second link stays off.
- r2c2=7, r3c3=4: r1c1, r1c2 and r5c5. The first link is off again, and the second still fires, because its triggers need entries and not light.

# Greek Carpet

A Greek carpet is a rolled path, commonly a spiral, paired with its straight, unrolled path. Read both from the corresponding starting end: their first digits match, their second digits match, and so on. The supplied paths must have the same length.

This uses the same position-by-position equality as cloned regions. The Greek carpet declaration records the ordered rolled and unrolled paths. A [Palindrome](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/palindrome.md) instead matches opposite positions on one path. Paths sharing a cell does not, by itself, make them a palindrome.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| line | The rolled path in order from its corresponding starting end. | Required. |
| unrolled | The corresponding cells on the unrolled path, in order. | Required. |

## Maths

Class: **first-order**.

The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate.

```text
|line|=|unrolled| ∧ ∀i∈[0,|line|): D(line[i])=D(unrolled[i])
```

Each path position matches the corresponding unrolled position in digit. Both paths have the same length.

## Example

setter: Example
source: ""
case: ""

status: read
---

```
````

Satisfies the rule: r1c1=1, r1c2=2, r1c4=2, r1c3=1. Corresponding positions contain matching digits.

Breaks the rule: r1c1=1, r1c2=2, r1c4=3, r1c3=1. The last corresponding digits differ.

For paths [r1c1,r1c2,r2c2] and [r1c1,r1c2,r1c3], the first two positions already coincide. The remaining condition is D(r2c2)=D(r1c3). Digits 1,2,3 on the first path and 1,2,3 on the second satisfy the correspondence, although neither sequence is a palindrome.

# Renban

The marked cells contain a consecutive run of values, in any order. Values are distinct by default. `repeats true` permits repeated values; `channel "D"` reads printed digits instead of effective values.

A cell set need not trace a path. With explicit `edges`, the rule applies once to the whole connected network, including every branch.

With `selection`, apply the rule to a stopping prefix of the ordered line. The prefix ends at the first target number, given or listed crust digit. `include` controls whether that cell is kept. A stopping cell must exist. Prefix selection uses the stated channel and an ordered line.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| selection | A stopping prefix, with its target or crust digits and inclusion policy. | Absent; use the whole cell set or network. |
| line | All cells of the line or cell set; order does not affect its consecutive values. | Required. |
| edges | Explicit undirected edges of one connected network; each edge lists two different cells. | Absent; use the ordered line. |
| channel | Read printed digits (D) or effective values (V). | V. |
| repeats | Whether equal values may repeat. | false. |

## Maths

Class: **with aggregates**.

The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate.

```text
if present(selection) then ¬present(edges) ∧ selectionValid(line,unwrap(selection),channel) ∧ consecutiveValues(selectedPrefix(line,unwrap(selection),channel),channel,repeats)
else lineGeometry(line,edges,false) ∧ (if present(edges) then consecutiveValues(graphVertices(unwrap(edges)),channel,repeats) else consecutiveValues(line,channel,repeats))
```

The whole supplied cell set or network component forms one consecutive set. Repeats are optional; every step between its least and greatest values is present.

Breaks the rule: r1c1=2, r1c2=1, r1c3=4. 2, 1, 4 misses 3 and has a gap in its run.

```rules

# Cage Shapes

Construct the hidden cages around their clues. Each cage has the stated size, includes its known cells, avoids free cells, and contains different digits adding to its total. Cages are connected and do not overlap.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| size | The number of cells in each constructed region or cage. | Required. |
| hidden | Each hidden cage: its clue cell, total and known member cells. | Required. |
| free | Cells excluded from all hidden cages. | Required. |

## Maths

Class: **existential**.

The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate.

```text
∃chosen:list<set<cell>>:
  |chosen|=|hidden|
  ∧ (∀i∈[0,|hidden|): let h=hidden[i]; let cageSet=chosen[i];
    |cageSet|=size ∧ cageSet⊆C ∧ connectedCells(cageSet) ∧ h.known⊆cageSet
    ∧ cageSet∩free=∅ ∧ h.clue∈cageSet ∧ (∀c∈cageSet: cellIndex(h.clue)<=cellIndex(c))
    ∧ distinct_D(cageSet) ∧ sum_D(cageSet)=h.sum)
  ∧ (∀i,j∈[0,|hidden|): i!=j → chosen[i]∩chosen[j]=∅)
```

There is one size-cell orthogonally connected shape for each hidden cage. It contains known, excludes free, starts at clue in reading order, has distinct digits totalling sum, and overlaps no other hidden cage. With hidden empty, this constraint adds no finished-grid condition.

# Battenburg

By default, every marked 2×2 square alternates between two classes across each edge, with equal classes on diagonals. Use face-digit parity or a shared selection. Exhaustive mode also forbids this pattern in unmarked squares wholly inside scope. Set `positive false` for marks that impose no positive condition. Every supplied mark must identify a complete square inside scope.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| marks | Zero-based top-left coordinates of marked squares. | Required. |
| scope | Cells on which squares may lie. | Required. |
| mode | The two-class source. | parity. |
| selectionRef | Selection name used in selection mode. | "H". |
| positive | Require marked squares to alternate. | true. |
| exhaustive | Forbid the pattern on unmarked squares inside scope. | false. |

The [shared predicates](predicates.md) define the notation and operations.

```text

# Lockout

The end digits differ by at least the stated gap. Every digit between them is below both ends or above both ends.

# Value Modifier

Choose modified cells according to the stated group counts. Their values are their digits times the factor, plus the offset. The same choices apply to every rule that reads values.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| name | The modifier name: doubler or negator. | Required. |
| factor | The multiplier for a modified digit. | Required. |
| offset | The amount added after multiplication. | Required. |
| exactly | The cells in each group and the exact number that must be modified. | Required. |
| count | The number of cells or occurrences to count. | Required. |
| atMostOne | The cells in each group that may contain at most one modified cell. | Required. |
| distinct | Whether modified cells must contain different digits. | Required. |

## Maths

Class: **existential**.

The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate.

```text
∃M:set<cell>: M⊆C ∧
(∀G∈exactly: |G∩M|=count) ∧ (∀G∈atMostOne: |G∩M|<=1)
∧ (distinct → distinct_D(M))
∧ (∀c∈C: (c∈M → V(c)=factor*D(c)+offset) ∧ (c∉M → V(c)=D(c)))
∧ (∀meaning∈ValuedRuleMeanings: meaning)
```

There is a shared set M of modified cells. Each exactly group intersects M in count cells; each atMostOne group intersects M in at most one. If distinct, digits in M are distinct. Every valued rule must accept V(c)=D(c)×factor+offset on M and D(c) elsewhere under this same M.

# Zipper

Pairs equally far from the centre have the same sum. By default, on an odd-length line that sum is the centre digit.

`centre "when-odd"` allows even and odd lengths, tying the pair sum to the centre only when it exists. `centre "ignore"` compares the mirrored pair sums without constraining an odd line’s centre. `centre "required"` requires odd length and ties every pair sum to the centre. Digits may repeat when other rules allow. A line with fewer than two cells has no pairs; only the required-centre version rejects empty or even length.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| centre | How the centre constrains pair sums and line length. | when-odd. |
| line | The cells in order, for example r1c1-r1c2-r1c3. | Required. |

## Maths

Class: **first-order**.

The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate.

```text
(∀i,j∈[0,|line|): i<⌊|line|/2⌋ ∧ j<⌊|line|/2⌋ → D(line[i])+D(line[|line|-1-i])=D(line[j])+D(line[|line|-1-j]))
∧ (centre="required" → |line| mod 2=1)
∧ (centre!="ignore" ∧ |line| mod 2=1 → ∀i∈[0,|line|): i<⌊|line|/2⌋ → |line|>0 ∧ 0<=⌊|line|/2⌋<|line| ∧ D(line[i])+D(line[|line|-1-i])=D(line[⌊|line|/2⌋]))
```

All mirrored pairs cells[i],cells[length−1−i] have the same sum. For odd length, each pair sums to the centre digit unless centre is ignore. The required mode also requires odd length.

## Example

case: ""

status: read
---

```

Satisfies the rule: r1c1=2, r1c2=5, r1c3=3. The end pair adds up to the centre digit 5.

Breaks the rule: r1c1=2, r1c2=5, r1c3=4. The end pair adds up to 6 instead of the centre digit 5.

### Choosing the centre rule

```rules
zipper r1c1-r2c2-r3c3-r4c4-r5c5 centre "ignore"
```

Satisfies the rule: [1,2,9,4,5] has pair sums 6 and 6; its centre 9 is ignored. Breaks the rule: [1,2,9,4,6] has unequal pair sums 7 and 6. The satisfying assignment fails the default centre rule.

With `centre "required"`, [1,2,6,4,5] satisfies the rule and [1,2,4,5] breaks it because its length is even. The latter satisfies `centre "when-odd"`.
